title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: scholidonline exposes small set user-facing functions: id_exists(x, type = NULL) id_convert(x, , = NULL) id_metadata(x, type = NULL) id_links(x, type = NULL) functions : Vectorized Type-stable Designed use pipelines Backed external registries Identifier detection normalization delegated internally scholid.

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_exists() verifies whether identifiers exist respective registries. type = NULL, type inferred automatically: Return values: TRUE → confirmed registry FALSE → confirmed found NA → classified normalized
code: scholidonline::id_exists(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) scholidonline::id_exists(   x = c(     "10.1000/182",     "12345678"   ) )

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: Many scholarly identifiers cross-linked across systems. Common examples: PMID → DOI PMCID → PMID arXiv → DOI (available) = NULL, source type inferred per element. Unresolvable mappings return NA_character_.
code: scholidonline::id_convert(   x    = "12345678",   from = "pmid",   to   = "doi" )

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_metadata() retrieves harmonized metadata external registries. Returned metadata registry-derived minimally harmonized across providers. Typical columns include: input type provider title year authors container doi pmid pmcid url Metadata completeness depends external authority.
code: scholidonline::id_metadata(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" )

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: id_links() returns related identifiers discovered via registry queries. may reveal: DOI PMID PMCID linked identifiers result long data.frame one row per link.
code: scholidonline::id_links(   x    = "PMC1234567",   type = "pmcid" )

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: common workflow messy identifier columns: Detect identifier types (via scholid). Normalize identifiers. Check registry existence. Convert enrich metadata. Example: separation keeps structural logic (scholid) registry logic (scholidonline) clearly distinct.
code: x <- c(   "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",   "PMID: 12345678",   "not an id" )  types <- scholid::detect_scholid_type(x) x_norm <- mapply(   scholid::normalize_scholid,   x    = x,   type = types,   SIMPLIFY = TRUE )  scholidonline::id_exists(x_norm, type = types)

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: functions accept provider argument. provider = "auto" (default), sensible registry chosen automatically. Available providers depend identifier type.
code: scholidonline::id_exists(   x        = "10.1000/182",   type     = "doi",   provider = "crossref" )

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: scholidonline relies external services: internet connection required. Rate limits may apply. Results may change time. Temporary failures can occur. reproducible workflows: Cache results appropriate. Record provider choices. Handle occasional NA values gracefully.

title: Getting started with scholidonline
text: scholid handles: Detection Normalization Classification Extraction scholidonline handles: Registry-backed validation Cross-system conversion Metadata retrieval Link discovery Together form clean two-layer design: Layer 1: Syntax canonical form Layer 2: External registry interaction

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: vignette explains means validate scholarly identifiers external registries scholidonline relates scholid. working identifiers programmatically, essential distinguish three levels validity: Structural validity Checksum validity Registry validity scholid operates structural (, applicable, checksum) level. scholidonline operates registry level. fundamentally different layers.

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: Structural validity answers: string match formal grammar identifier system? Example: Structural validation uses regular expressions , applicable, checksum algorithms (e.g., ORCID). require internet access. confirm existence.
code: scholid::is_scholid("10.1000/182", type = "doi")

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: Registry validity answers: identifier exist external authority? example: DOI resolve via doi.org Crossref? PMID exist PubMed? ORCID iD present ORCID registry? Example: Registry validation: Requires internet access Depends external APIs May affected rate limits temporary outages Can change time structurally valid identifier may still fail registry validation.
code: scholidonline::id_exists("10.1000/182", type = "doi")

title: Online Resolution and Registry Validation
text: function id_exists() performs registry-backed validation. Example: Possible return values: TRUE → confirmed registry FALSE → registry confirms found NA → input classified normalized Importantly, NA mean “exist”. means “evaluated”.
code: scholidonline::id_exists(   x    = "12345678",   type = "pmid" )

text: Many scholarly identifiers linked across systems. Examples: PMID → DOI PMCID → PMID arXiv → DOI (available) id_convert() performs registry-backed crosswalks. title: Online Resolution, Conversion, and Metadata for Scholarly Identifiers
text: detailed usage patterns check Get started vignette.
code: # list supported scholarly identifier types scholid::scholid_types() ## [1] "arxiv" "doi"   "isbn"  "issn"  "orcid" "pmcid" "pmid" # test whether values match a given identifier type scholid::is_scholid(   x    = "10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ## [1] TRUE # normalize identifiers to canonical form scholid::normalize_scholid(   x    = "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",   type = "doi" ) ## [1] "10.1000/182" # extract identifiers of a given type from free text scholid::extract_scholid(   text = "See https://doi.org/10.1000/182 for details.",   type = "doi" ) ## [[1]] ## [1] "10.1000/182" # classify the identifier type of each input value scholid::classify_scholid(   x = c(     "10.1000/182",     "0000-0002-1825-0097",     "not an id"   ) ) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" NA # detect identifier types from canonical or wrapped input values scholid::detect_scholid_type(   x = c(     "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",     "ORCID: 0000-0002-1825-0097",     "arXiv:2101.00001",     "not an id"   ) ) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" "arxiv" NA
